name: Tuna biscuits
description: Small homemade tuna biscuits baked until firm. Designed as an occasional treat, not a complete meal.

ingredients.name: Canned tuna in spring water, drained

steps: Preheat the oven to 180 C and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Drain the tuna thoroughly and mash it with a fork.
Combine the tuna with the egg, oat flour and sunflower oil.
Add a little water if needed and form a workable dough.
Shape into small biscuits and bake for 12-15 minutes. Allow to cool completely before serving.
tip: Choose tuna in spring water rather than brine and keep portions small. These biscuits are an occasional treat.

name: Chicken biscuits
description: Homemade biscuits made with plain cooked chicken, egg and rice flour. Serve occasionally as a treat.
steps: Preheat the oven to 175 C and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Finely chop or blend the plain cooked chicken.
Mix in the egg, yogurt and sunflower oil.
Gradually incorporate the rice flour until a dough forms.
Shape into small biscuits and bake for about 20 minutes. Cool completely before serving.
tip: Use only plain cooked chicken with no salt, sauces, onion, garlic or seasoning.

name: Tuna mini-cake
description: A small soft tuna cake made with egg and a little plain soft cheese. An occasional homemade treat for cats.

ingredients.name: Canned tuna in spring water, drained

steps: Preheat the oven to 180 C.
Drain the tuna thoroughly and break it into small pieces.
Mix the tuna with the egg and soft cheese until combined.
Transfer the mixture to a small muffin mould.
Bake until completely set, then allow to cool before serving.
tip: Serve only a small portion. Dairy can cause digestive upset in some cats, so a lactose-free product is preferable.

name: Frozen tuna bites
description: Simple frozen bites made from tuna and water. A refreshing occasional treat served in very small portions.

ingredients.name: Canned tuna in spring water, drained

steps: Drain the tuna thoroughly.
Blend the tuna with the water until smooth.
Spoon the mixture into a small silicone mould or ice cube tray.
Freeze until completely solid.
Remove one small portion and let it soften slightly before offering it to your cat.
tip: Make the portions very small and allow them to soften before serving rather than giving your cat a large hard-frozen piece.

name: Frozen wet food bites
description: Your cat's usual wet food transformed into small frozen treats with a little added water.

ingredients.name: Your cat's usual complete wet food

steps: Place the wet food in a bowl.
Mix in the water until the texture becomes smooth and slightly looser.
Divide the mixture between small silicone moulds.
Freeze until firm.
Let a portion soften slightly before serving.
tip: Using your cat's usual complete wet food avoids introducing unnecessary new ingredients. Keep the portions small.

name: Chicken & zucchini
description: Tender shredded chicken combined with soft cooked zucchini and a little water for extra moisture.
steps: Cook the chicken thoroughly in plain water or steam it without salt, oil or seasoning.
Steam the zucchini until very soft.
Finely shred the chicken and chop or mash the zucchini into small pieces.
Mix the ingredients and add a little water for a moist texture.
Allow to cool to room temperature before serving.
tip: This is a complementary homemade dish, not a nutritionally complete everyday diet. Serve occasionally alongside a complete cat food.

name: Salmon & pumpkin
description: Flaked cooked salmon mixed with tender pumpkin for a soft and simple homemade dish.
steps: Cook the salmon thoroughly by steaming or baking it without salt, oil or seasoning.
Cook the pumpkin until completely soft.
Flake the salmon carefully and check again that no bones remain.
Mash or dice the pumpkin into small pieces and combine it with the salmon.
Add a little water for extra moisture and allow to cool before serving.
tip: Check the salmon carefully for bones. This recipe should be offered as an occasional complementary dish rather than a complete daily meal.
